revision_notes: Light check surfaced a clearly authoritative source — an official Civil Status Division (Prime Minister's Office) presentation at ID4Africa 2019 — describing automatic technical linkage between birth/death registration and the National Identity Number (NIN): a NIN is computer-generated at birth registration, and the same ID is de-activated at death. This directly contradicts the original 'no evidence' Unknown score, so the row was escalated to full verification and the underlying Civil Status Act (2023 consolidation) was checked to confirm the legal basis for this linkage remains current.
revised_comments: Mauritius's civil registration system is fully and automatically integrated with the national identity system. A unique National Identity Number (NIN) is computer-generated at the point of birth registration in the Central Civil Status Office system, and the same identity number is de-activated upon registration of death, closing the identity lifecycle. This integration is described by the Civil Status Division (Prime Minister's Office) as a core feature of Mauritius's civil registration and vital statistics ecosystem, underpinned by the Civil Status Act 1981 and National Identity Card Act 1986.
